title: Redis performance optimisation
context: How do you keep Redis fast in production?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Keep commands cheap: avoid KEYS and SMEMBERS on huge sets, use SCAN for iteration, and bound list and sorted-set sizes. Batch round trips with pipelining or MGET, and use Lua scripts or transactions to make multi-step changes atomic. Watch for big keys, which block the main thread when deleted, and use UNLINK or lazy freeing. Use connection pools in the app, and monitor latency with SLOWLOG and LATENCY. Spread load with replicas and sharding.

points.title: Avoid O(n) commands
points.why: KEYS and large range reads block every other client while they run.

points.title: Batch round trips
points.why: Pipelining and MGET cut network time, which is often the real cost.

points.title: Big keys
points.why: Deleting a huge key blocks the main thread. UNLINK frees it in the background.
